Feature: Register Default Value and Write/Read Verification
Test Description: This test case verifies the register accessibility and data integrity of 434 registers across the DWC Ethernet QoS IP (ethernet1). The test validates two fundamental aspects of register behavior: (1) that all registers hold their expected default (reset) values after power-on, and (2) that writable register fields correctly accept, store, and return written data patterns while read-only fields retain their default values. The test covers registers spanning the MAC, MMC, MTL (including per-queue registers for queues 0-3), and DMA (including per-channel registers for channels 0-3) functional blocks. Registers are selectively skipped based on predefined skip arrays for both default value checking and write/read checking phases. The test uses read masks and write masks to account for read-only, write-only, and reserved bit fields within each register.
Test Steps / Procedure:
Phase 1 - Default Value Verification:
1. Iterate through all 434 registers in the register address array.
2. For each register, check if the register is readable (non-zero read mask). Skip non-readable registers.
3. Check if the register is marked for skipping in the reset-skip array. Skip if flagged.
4. Read the current value of the register.
5. Compare the read value against the expected default value from the default value array.
6. If mismatch, increment the default-fail counter and log the failure with register identity, expected value, and actual read value.

Phase 2 - Write/Read Pattern Verification:
7. For each of 6 data patterns (all-ones, alternating-AA, alternating-55, all-zeros, alternating-A5, upper-half-ones), perform steps 8-13.
8. Write Phase: Iterate through all 434 registers. Skip registers flagged in the skip array. Skip registers with zero write mask (non-writable). Write the current data pattern to each eligible register.
9. Read Phase: Iterate through all 434 registers. Skip registers flagged in the skip array. Skip registers with zero write mask. Skip registers with zero read mask (non-readable).
10. Read the current value of each eligible register.
11. Compute the expected value by combining the written data pattern (masked by both read mask and write mask) with the default value for read-only bits (masked by the inverted write mask and read mask).
12. Compare the read value against the computed expected value.
13. If mismatch, increment the write-fail counter and log the failure with register identity, expected value, and actual read value.

Phase 3 - Final Verdict:
14. If either the default-fail counter or write-fail counter is greater than zero, signal test failure.
15. Otherwise, signal test success.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1. Default Value Check: Every readable register (not flagged for skip in the reset-skip array) must return its documented default value when read after power-on reset.

2. Write/Read Pattern Check: For each of the 6 test data patterns, every writable and readable register (not flagged for skip in the skip array) must return the expected value after a write operation.

3. Overall Pass/Fail: The test passes (finish with success) if and only if both the default-fail counter and the write-fail counter remain at zero after all phases complete.
Remarks: The test covers 434 registers across MAC, MMC, MTL (queues 0-3), and DMA (channels 0-3) blocks of the DWC Ethernet QoS IP. A soft reset check function is defined in the source but is commented out and not executed in the active test flow.

Feature: Basic TX (Transmit) Operation with Interrupt Handling
Test Description: This test case verifies the basic transmit (TX) operation of the DWC Ethernet QoS IP (ethernet1) using DMA channel 0. The test validates the end-to-end TX data path by configuring MAC address registers with DMA channel selection and address enable for 4 MAC addresses, setting up the MAC packet filter for hash filtering and receive-all mode, enabling TX and RX in full duplex mode via the MAC Configuration register, programming all 4 MTL TX queues with store-and-forward mode and queue sizes, configuring quantum weights for TX queue scheduling, enabling RX queue overflow and TX queue underflow interrupts on all 4 MTL queues, configuring the DMA system bus mode for outstanding requests and burst selection, preloading TX descriptors, programming DMA channel TX descriptor ring lengths, list base addresses, and tail pointers for all 4 channels, configuring DMA channel controls, enabling DMA channel interrupts for all 4 channels, and initiating TX on DMA channel 0.
Test Steps / Procedure:
Step 1 - MAC Address Configuration:
1. Configure MAC Address3 High register with address enable, DMA channel 3 selection, and upper MAC address bits.
2. Configure MAC Address2 High register with address enable, DMA channel 2 selection, and upper MAC address bits.
3. Configure MAC Address1 High register with address enable, DMA channel 1 selection, and upper MAC address bits.
4. Configure MAC Address0 High register with address enable, DMA channel 0 selection, and upper MAC address bits.
5. Configure MAC Address3 Low through MAC Address0 Low registers with lower 32-bit MAC address values.

Step 2 - MAC Configuration:
6. Configure MAC Packet Filter register to enable hash filtering and receive-all mode.
7. Configure MAC Configuration register to enable TX and RX with full duplex mode and speed selection.
8. Configure MAC Extended Configuration register with default settings.

Step 3 - MTL TX Queue Configuration:
9. Configure MTL TxQ3 through TxQ0 Operation Mode registers with TX queue size (4096 bytes) and store-and-forward mode.
10. Configure MTL TxQ3 through TxQ0 Quantum Weight registers with scheduling weight values.
11. Configure MTL Q3 through Q0 Interrupt Control Status registers to enable RX queue overflow and TX queue underflow interrupts.

Step 8 - Start TX:
20. Start TX on DMA channel 0 by writing to the DMA CH0 TX Control register.

Step 9 - Interrupt-Driven Polling:
21. Enter a polling loop (10 iterations). In each iteration, wait for the transfer complete interrupt.

Step 10 - Test Completion:
24. Signal test success.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1. MAC Address Configuration: MAC Address0 through Address3 High and Low registers must be successfully written.

2. TX Operation: After starting TX on DMA channel 0, the DMA engine must process TX descriptors and generate transfer complete interrupts.

3. Interrupt Polling: The test must successfully complete 10 interrupt-driven polling iterations.

4. Test Completion: The test signals success upon completing all 10 interrupt cycles.
Remarks: TX is started only on DMA channel 0 in this test. TX start for DMA channels 1, 2, and 3 is defined in the source but is inactive (commented out). The test uses a preload descriptor mechanism to set up TX descriptors in memory before starting the DMA engine.
